Q: Play Framework's Json.format not working with our models after upgrading to Scala 3? A:

I don't think you missed a migration step in play-json. Json.format[X] in Scala 3 fails with Fails to resolve field: '...X._1' when the case class X was compiled by Scala 2.13. The macro call compiles in Scala 3, but the class comes from a module or artifact that is still on 2.13. This is a common state in a partial migration of a large codebase.

You traced the error to the correct place, but the missing piece is one level up, in JsMacroImpl.scala:521:

productWrites[t, t](config, forwardExpr.asExprOf[OWrites[t]], '{ identity[t] }, pof)

For a case class, the macro passes identity as the "convert to Product" function. Thus the "tuple type" that reaches QuotesHelper is not a real tuple. The "tuple type" is Country itself. Then QuotesHelper.scala:129-140 looks up the synthetic product accessors _1, _2, and so on, as declared members of Country:

val field = tupleTpeSym.declaredField(fieldNme)          // "_1", "_2", ...
if field == Symbol.noSymbol then {
  tupleTpeSym.declaredMethod(fieldNme) match {
    case meth :: Nil => ...
    case _ =>
      report.errorAndAbort(s"Fails to resolve field: '${tupleTpeSym.fullName}.${fieldNme}'")

A case class from the Scala 3 compiler declares these _1..._N methods. A case class from the Scala 2.13 compiler does not declare them in the metadata that the Scala 3 macro reads. Thus declaredMethod("_1") finds nothing, and the macro stops with your exact error.

I reproduced with play-json 3.0.6:

package net.group.rest.member
case class Country(code: String, name: String)

import play.api.libs.json.*
implicit val fmt: OFormat[Country] = Json.format[Country]
  • Both files compiled with Scala 3 (tested 3.3.6, 3.6.4, 3.7.3, 3.8.4): works.
  • Country packaged into a jar with Scala 2.13.16, the format compiled with Scala 3.3.6: Fails to resolve field: 'net.group.rest.member.Country._1': the exact error.
  • The same jar recompiled with Scala 3.3.6: works again.

Custom apply, custom unapply, one-field classes, private constructors, and trait parents do not seem to cause this error.

Country almost certainly comes from a place that is still on Scala 2.13:

  • A subproject that does not yet set scalaVersion to 3, while the module with the Json.format call does.
  • A dependency that resolves to a _2.13 artifact, for example through CrossVersion.for3Use2_13.

Run sbt "show <module>/Compile/dependencyClasspath" and search for _2.13 jars (or 2.13 class output) that contain your model classes.

The cleanest possible fix, if possible, is to migrate the module that defines the case classes to Scala 3 first. Then migrate the modules that call Json.format on them. The macro then works unchanged. The general rule: with play-json, migrate leaf model modules before the modules that derive formats for them.

Q: Spring - Stop a background task running on port 8080 A:
  • Open the command prompt as Adminstrator
  • Run the command taskkill /PID <PID> /F /T

Q: Terminating Flask app by Ctrl+C does not trigger KeyboardInterrupt A:

as @jonsharpe assumes, the app.run is being controlled by the built in debugger and its handling the ^C functionality you're hoping to trap. (@furas also alluded to) (https://flask.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/debugging/) not sure why you need debug=True , here's your code with it set to False ... for demonstration purposes .

If you share why its set to True perhaps we can assist more...

cat /tmp/flakyFlask.py
from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/')
def hello_world():
    return 'Hello, World!'

if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        print(1111111)
        app.run(debug=False,load_dotenv=False)
        print(2222222)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print(3333333)

% python3 /tmp/flakyFlask.py
1111111

 * Debug mode: off
WARNING: This is a development server. Do not use it in a production deployment. Use a production WSGI server instead.

Press CTRL+C to quit
